source.title: Watermarking Degrades Alignment in Language Models: Analysis and Mitigation
source.authors: Apurv Verma; H. Phan; Shubhendu Trivedi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures harmful-response behavior after inference-time watermarking changes token selection, a different decoding intervention from the claim’s fine-tuning, prefilling, and suffix examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports safety outcomes under KGW and Gumbel watermarking. Cited results about fine-tuning, jailbreaks, and other work are not study results and are not recorded as rows. The paper also reports reward-guided resampling results, but that procedure is intended to restore alignment rather than bypass refusal, so those results are not rows for V4.
record.test_reason: The study measures how often instruction-tuned models give unsafe responses to 3,819 harmful prompts under two inference-time decoding changes (KGW and Gumbel watermarking), compared with unwatermarked decoding. That bears directly on V4's claim that decoding changes defeat refusal. The setting is new (watermarked sampling) rather than a method aimed at the shallow-alignment question, so T3 fits better than T2. No row looks at response position, prefills or suffixes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that watermarking shifts alignment in model-specific ways: guard attenuation (more unsafe responses) or guard amplification (overrefusal), plus lower truthfulness. These shifts persist after controlling for perplexity. Reward-guided Best-of-N resampling with 2 to 4 samples restores or exceeds unwatermarked alignment without hurting watermark detection.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is inference-time watermarking that alters token selection, not fine-tuning, compliant-opening prefilling, or adversarial suffixes.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by model and watermarking method; the paper also reports effects of watermark strength and sampling temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger watermarks (higher KGW δ or higher temperature) lower ArmoRM reward scores for LLaMA-8B-Inst (Figures 6a and 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The degree of decoding perturbation scales alignment degradation, measured by a reward score rather than a harmful-compliance rate.

record.problems: Safety outcomes relevant here are mostly described qualitatively or shown in figures, without uncertainty estimates. Effects vary by model and watermarking scheme, and the paper does not test prefills or suffixes.
record.rows_left_out: Reward-guided Best-of-N resampling outcomes in Sections 4-5 and Appendices J, K, and O are omitted because the intervention selects for alignment rather than testing a bypass of refusal. Additional extended-model figure results are not separately catalogued because the text and figure captions do not consistently agree on the direction of the safety changes.

untested.parts: Prefilling a compliant opening, adversarial suffixes, and whether the watermark's effect operates through the first response tokens.
All of it: no harmful fine-tuning.
All of it: no benign fine-tuning.
All of it: no per-token KL by position.
All of it: no parameter localization.
All of it: no analysis of the causes of shallowness.
All of it: the mitigation is Best-of-N resampling, not training that deepens alignment.

missing.what: Unsafe-response changes under KGW and Gumbel for Qwen2.5-14B (guard amplification under KGW), Mistral-Small-24B and Gemma-27B (guard attenuation under both schemes).
Scaling across Qwen2.5 1.5B to 14B: KGW unsafe responses fall with scale while Gumbel unsafe responses rise with scale.
Per-category unsafe counts for the four main models (for example, economic harm up to +200 and malware +75 under KGW).

record.verdict_notes: The watermark changes decoding throughout the response and is not aimed at bypassing refusal. The paper does not connect its effect to the opening tokens, so it bears only on the 'decoding changes' clause of V4. The rows_left_out claim that the extended-model figures and text disagree is only partly true: Mistral-Small and Gemma agree across text and captions, and the conflict concerns Qwen2.5-14B under KGW. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The magnitudes for the main models are in figures only.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence by response position.
The study tests watermarking-induced token-selection changes, not compliant-opening prefills or adversarial suffixes; it does not measure whether effects are concentrated in initial response tokens.
Localization of safety behavior in weights, parameters, or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety across response positions and its robustness.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen2-7B under KGW and Gumbel watermarking at τ=1.0
relationships.reason: Watermarked decoding raises unsafe responses (Qwen2-7B by only +1.2% and +3.9%; the LLaMA and Mistral rises are unquantified in the text, with category rises of up to about 200 of 3,819 prompts), so refusal is eroded but not defeated (r1-r6).
relationships.display_finding: Watermarked decoding increases unsafe responses, by only +1.2% and +3.9% for Qwen2-7B and by up to about 200 of 3,819 prompts in single categories, so refusal erodes but is not defeated.

relationships.display_finding: Mistral-Small-24B and Gemma-27B give more unsafe responses under watermarking, while Qwen2.5-14B under KGW is described as becoming more cautious, so the direction depends on the model.

source_check.reason: Retain limits_scope for Mistral-Small-24B and Gemma-27B under both schemes, and separate Qwen2.5-14B under KGW into its own condition group. Appendix J.2 explicitly reports increased unsafe responses for Mistral and Gemma, but describes only increased cautiousness for Qwen; this alone does not establish reversed unsafe responses. Figures 18 and 20 captions also claim unsafe responses increase across all extended models, leaving Qwen's V4 direction unresolved.

relation.reason: The study measures whether decoding perturbations increase harmful compliance, including conditions where unsafe responses instead decrease.

tranche.reason: Inference-time watermarking supplies a new setting with direct measurements of unsafe responses relative to unwatermarked decoding, bearing on V4.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper describes increased unsafe responses (guard attenuation) for these models under watermarking, though it does not quantify the increases here; see r1-r4.
